property_summary: General rule: when the caller is the owner, sendTo should not revert (i.e., !reverted || (amount == 0)).

For any caller and any nonzero amount, when the owner calls sendTo with that amount the contract's balance decreases (transfer succeeds); the mutant that requires amount==0 prevents nonzero transfers, so there exist inputs (nonzero amount by owner) where the mutant fails and the reference succeeds.

For any caller and any amount, if the caller is the owner and the contract has at least `amount` balance, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) does not revert (i.e. succeeds); the mutant adding `require(amount == 0)` makes some owner/nonzero-amount calls revert, violating this property.

For every caller and amount, if the caller is the owner and the contract holds at least `amount` wei, then calling sendTo(receiver, amount) succeeds (does not revert) on the reference; the mutant that requires `amount == 0` causes some owner calls with nonzero amounts to revert, breaking this rule.

For any receiver address and any non-negative amount, if the caller is the contract owner and the contract has at least that amount of ETH, then after calling sendTo(receiver, amount) the contract's balance decreases by exactly amount (i.e., transfer of arbitrary amount succeeds and funds are moved) — the mutant that forces amount == 0 breaks this when amount != 0.

For any caller that is the owner and any receiver/address and any amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) on the correct contract never reverts when the contract has at least amount wei (i.e., it always succeeds for owner calls); the mutant that adds require(amount == 0) causes owner calls with nonzero amount to revert, violating this rule.

For any caller who is the owner and any nonzero amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) always increases receiver's balance by exactly amount in the correct contract; the mutant that uses transfer(amount - 1) can increase it by one wei less (or revert when amount == 0).

For any caller who is the contract owner and any amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) always increases receiver's balance by exactly amount (and never reverts for amount>0); the mutant sending amount-1 either increases by one wei less or reverts when amount==0, violating this rule.

For any owner caller and any nonzero amount sent with enough balance, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) succeeds and increases receiver's balance by exactly amount; the mutant that transfers amount-1 either reverts for amount==0 or increases by one wei less for amount>0, breaking this equality.

For any caller that is the contract owner and any receiver address and uint256 amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) never decreases the contract's balance by more than amount (i.e., the contract's balance decreases by exactly amount when call succeeds); the mutant that transfers amount-1 causes the contract balance to decrease by less than amount for some inputs (and may revert when amount==0).

For every caller equal to the contract owner and every amount > 0 sent as msg.value from the owner to the contract then invoking sendTo(receiver, amount) never reverts and causes receiver's balance to increase by exactly amount; the mutant that transfers amount-1 will either revert when amount==0 or increase receiver balance by one wei less for some amount>0, violating this equality.

For any caller who is the owner and any positive amount up to the contract balance, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) should transfer the funds out of the contract to the provided receiver so address(c).balance decreases by amount (the buggy mutant sends to owner instead, so address(c).balance behavior differs for some inputs).

For any caller who is the contract owner and any amount <= contract balance, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) preserves that the contract's balance decreases by exactly amount (i.e., address(c).balance after the call = before - amount); the mutant that transfers to owner instead of receiver can violate this observable balance change for some inputs.

For any sender who is the contract owner and any amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) on the correct contract reduces the contract's balance by exactly amount (the buggy mutant that transfers to owner instead of receiver can cause the call to revert when receiver is a contract that rejects funds, producing a different observable outcome — a revert — for some inputs).

For any receiver address and amount that the owner sends as call value to C.sendTo when the contract has >= amount balance, the reference always forwards Ether to the provided receiver (so receiver's balance increases by amount), whereas the mutant forwards to owner instead, so there exist inputs where the receiver's balance does not increase by that amount.

For any owner caller and any receiver that is a contract which reverts on receiving Ether, the reference C will forward funds to that receiver (causing the sendTo call to revert), whereas the mutant that sends to owner instead will not revert in that case — so the reference always reverts when receiver reverts, but the mutant sometimes succeeds; thus the rule: if receiver's fallback/receive reverts, then sendTo call should revert for all inputs with msg.sender==owner and amount>0.
